figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Diels-Alderases catalyzed reactions.  a) SAM-dependent LepI catalyzed hetero-Diels–
Alder (hDA) and retro-Claisen reaction in the biosynthesis of leporin B27; b) EpiI (or its homologues 
UpiI and HpiI) catalyzes hDA reaction to form asperpyridone A, and PdxI (or its homologues AdxI 
and ModxI) catalyzes Alder-ene reaction to form pyridoxatin28; c) NgnD (or its homologues StmD 
and 10105D) catalyzed [4+2]/ [6+4] cycloaddition in the biosynthesis of streptoseomycin29; d) SpnF 
catalyzed [4+2] cycloaddition in the biosynthesis of spinosyn A30; e) Combination of PyrE3 and PyrI4 
catalyzed [4+2] cyclization cascade to form pyrroindomycins31; f) Tsn11 catalyzed inverse-electron-
demand hDA reaction and Tsn15 catalyzed pericyclic rearrangement reaction in the biosynthesis of 
tetronasin32.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Complex natural products probably biosynthesized via cascade intermolecular Diels-
Alder cycloadditions33-41.  a) Examples of dimeric or trimeric natural products; b) bistropolone-sesquiterpenes 
and their derivatives42. Eupenifeldin series (i) and pycnidione series (ii) are probably biosynthesized via tandem 
intermolecular Diels-Alder cycloadditions. The absolute configurations of pycnidione subclass were adapted from 
the latest reference25.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Summary of synthetic efforts to humulene-containing meroterpenoids. a) 
Synthesis of mono-hDA products43-45; b) Synthesis of bis-hDA analogs25,46,47. So far, total 
chemical synthesis of natural eupenifeldin (1)23 and pycnidione (1')  has not been achieved.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. Combinatorial heterologous biosynthesis. a) Exchange of eupfF and eupfG in A. nidulans 
co-expressing eupfABCDEFG (produce compounds 1, 2, 4, 8, and 9) to pycR1 and asR6, respectively, 
afforded expected pycnidione (1'), together with epolone B (2'), compound 4', ring-contraction 
products 8' and epolone A (9') (i and ii). For the detection of compounds 4 and 4', ion chromatograms 
ESI + m/z = 203 for 4 and 4' were extracted. However, replacement of eupfF or eupfG alone not only 
dramatically reduces the output of the products but also effect the production of bis-hDA products (iii 
and iv).  b) Structures of compounds isolated from heterologous biosynthesis. These compounds were 
identified by comparison of NMR data with those reported (Supplementary Figures 37-73 and 
Supplementary Tables 12-19).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. LC-MS analysis of the metabolites from A. nidulans transformants and feeding 
experiments. a) The culture of A. nidulans co-expressing eupfABCDEFG in liquid CD-ST medium for 
3-5 days (traces i-iii), led to the major production of 1 and 2. The targeted bistropolone-sesquiterpenoid 
1 was largely accumulated from day 4 (trace ii). Feeding 4 (trace iv) or 2 (trace v) to A. nidulans co-
expressing eupfABCEF generated major of 1 and a tiny of 9. Feeding water-soluble 8 to A. nidulans 
co-expressing eupfABCDEF (trace vi) or containing empty victor (trace vii) did not generate additional 
products, suggesting that 8 was not a biosynthetic precursor of 9. However, 1 could not convert to 9 in 
A. nidulans co-expressing eupfABCDEF (traces viii and ix), probably due to its insolubility in water, 
which hinder it enter the host. All feeding experiments were carried out on day 4, and metabolites were 
detected on day 5. b) A concise proposed biosynthetic pathway for compounds 1, 2, 8, and 9.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 7
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 7. Subcellular localization of proteins from eupf BGC. a) Examination of EupfA-sfGFP, 
EupfB-sfGFP, EupfC-sfGFP, EupfD-sfGFP, EupfE-sfGFP and EupfG-sfGFP fusion proteins in A. 
nidulans by laser scanning confocal microscopy. Green fluorescence indicates that they all localizes 
to the cytoplasm and intracellular organelles. The strains were cultured in CD agar media (enlarged 
at 20  10, scale bar = 50 μm). b) Subcellular localization of the EupfF-sfGFP fusion proteins in A. 
nidulans. Green fluorescence indicates that EupfF-sfGFP localizes to the apical media (red arrows) 
and septa (white arrows). The strain was cultured in agar plates (enlarged at 20  10, scale bar = 50 
μm) or broth media (enlarged at 40  10, scale bar = 20 μm).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 8
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 8. Characterization of EupfF as secreted protein. a) SDS-PAGE gel (12%) of the broth of 
A. nidulans overexpressing various combination of genes eupfABCEF, eupfABCDEF, eupfBCDEF, 
eupfDEF, eupfEF, eupfF, and eupfE, as well as empty vectors (UPR). M: protein marker of Prestained 
Protein Ladder from PageRulerTM, product #26616. b) Biotransformation of medium from A. 
nidulans co-expressing eupfF using i) 6 and 4 or iii) 6 and 2 as co-substrates. Control (ii and iv): 
substrates incubation with medium of strains containing empty vectors. These results show that EupfF 
is a secreted protein with TDA catalytic activity.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 9
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 9. The culture time-dependent proteins purification. SDS-PAGE gel (12%) of mycelia and 
broth of A. nidulans strains co-expressing eupfF (a) or pycR1 (b). The results showed that protein 
secretion mainly accumulated on day 4. M: protein marker of Prestained Protein Ladder from 
PageRulerTM, product #26616.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 10
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 10. Effects of temperature, pH and divalent metal ions on the activity of EupfF and 
PycR1. The reaction mixtures containing 20 μM pre-diene 6, and a) 10 μM 4 with 1 μM EupfF; or b) 
10 μM 2 with 1 μM EupfF; or c) 10 μM 4' with 1 μM PycR1; or D) 10 μM 2' with 1 μM PycR1 were 
incubated in various conditions. Left column: pH 7.2-7.4, temperature varied from 8°C to 75 °C; 
middle column: pH varied from 3 to 11, temperature 28 °C; right column: pH 7.2-7.4, temperature 
28 °C, with additional 2 mM divalent metal such as Ca2+, Ni2+, Mg2+, Mn2+, Cu2+, Zn2+, Co2+, or 
Fe2+after treatment with 50 mM EDTA disodium salt for 30 mins (to exclude the effect of inherent 
Ca2+in the proteins, the fresh purified protein samples were dialyzed extensively with buffer 
containing 50 mM EDTA disodium salt in 15ml ultrafiltration device for three times). In the EDTA 
control, dialysis buffer containing 10 mM EDTA disodium salt was used. Enzyme activity values 
represent mean ± s.d. of three independent replicates. The results showed that the optimal temperature 
of the protein was 28 °C, and the optimal PH range was pH 6-8. The catalytic activity of the protein 
mainly depended on calcium ions, while the presence of magnesium and manganese ions could also 
retain weak activities.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 11
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 11. The time-course in vitro assay for EupfF and PycR1. Compounds 6 and 4 (or 2) were 
incubated with EupfF, and compounds 6 and 4' (or 2') were incubated with PycR1. The 100 μL 
reaction mixtures containing 10 μM EupfF or 5 μM PycR1, 50 mM PBS (pH 7.2-7.4), 100 μM pre-
diene 6, and 100 μM 4 (4') or 2 (2') were incubated at 28 °C for 90 min. The reactions were 
terminated by the addition of 400 μL of EtOAc and were extracted for three times. The supernatants 
were concentrated by vacuum and then dissolved in 30 μl acetonitrile before analyzed by the 
UPLC/MS.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 12
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 12. Verification of the optimum substrates for EupfF and PycR1. a) A final volume of 
100 μL reaction mixtures containing 1 μM EupfF or PycR1, 50 mM PBS at pH 7.2-7.4, 10 μM pre-
diene 6, and i) 10 μM 4 and 10 μM 2', or ii) 10 μM 4' and 10 μM 2, or iii) 10 μM 4 and 10 μM 2', or 
iv) 10 μM 4' and 10 μM 2, were incubated at 28 °C for 90 min. In the case of EupfF, it showed that 1 
was the major bis-hDA product, which was derived from 4 (see trace i). Similarly, in the case of 
PycR1 (trave iv), 4' was more efficiently converted to bis-hDA product 1'. Based on these results, we 
can conclude that these hDAases prefer to recognize the substrate 4/4' to form mono-hDA and 
resultant bis-hDA products. b) The time course reactions for EupfF or PycR1 with oversupplied 6 
(100 μM). The 100 μL reaction mixtures containing 50 mM PBS (pH 7.2-7.4), 100 μM pre-diene 6, 
10 μM 4 (or 4'), and 1 μM EupfF or PycR1 were incubated at 28 °C for 5 - 60 min. With excessive 
pre-diene 6 supplied, 4 and 4' were mainly converted to 1 and 1', respectively, while 2/2' were almost 
indetectable.

figure_candidates.caption:

of pre-diene 6, 5-500 μM of 4 (4') or 2 (2'), and varying concentrations of enzymes in 50 mM PBS 
buffer at pH 7.2 - 7.4 were incubated at 28 °C for 5 mins. The enzymes used in the reactions were 
1 μM EupfF (a, b, e, f), or 1 μM PycR1 (c), or 0.2 μM PycR1 (d), or 0.5 μM PycR1 (g, h). The results

figure_candidates.label: Figure 14
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 14. Predication of N-Glycosylation sites in EupfF and PycR1. The sequence context of 
Asn-Xaa-Ser/Thr sequons were examined using the online NetNGlyc 1.0 Server at www.cbs.dtu.dk. 
The prediction results showed that there were four potential N-glycosylation sites (N45, N68, N213, 
and N300) in EupfF, and two potential N-glycosylation sites (N43 and N49) in PycR1. However, the 
predicted N-glycosylation sites at N49 in PycR1 was not observed in crystal structure and LC-MS/MS 
analysis. Moreover, N-glycan at N211 in PycR1 was observed.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 15
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 15. Characterization of EupfF and PycR1 as glycoproteins with N-glycans. Periodic Acid-
Schiff (PAS) Staining (a) and Coomassie blue staining (b, c) of SDS-PAGE (12%) of EupfF, PycR1 
and their mutants. Peptide-N-Glycosidase F (PNGase F) was used to remove high mannose N-glycans 
from glycoproteins. Red circles showed the proteins with N-glycans. The amount of protein secretions 
of WT and mutants were distinctly different (d). Yield values of protein represent mean ± s.d. of three 
independent replicates. M: protein marker of Prestained Protein Ladder from PageRulerTM, product 
#26616.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 16
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 16. Ca ion is important for dehydration of 6. a) LC-MS analysis of the products from in 
vitro assays of PycR1 (containing Ca2+) or 0.1 M EDTA pre-treated PycR1 (Ca2+ removed) using 6 
and 4' as substrates. The 100 μL reaction mixtures containing 50 mM PBS at pH 7.2-7.4, 1 mM pre-
diene 6, 1 mM 4', 50 μM protein (containing 20% glycerol) were incubated at 28 °C for 90 min. 2 
mM CaCl2 was added to the reaction mixtures in iii) and vi); b) Schematic diagram of the reaction 
route including: a) 6 was captured by glycerol to form by-product 6a22; or b) dehydration of 6 to form 
diene 7, and 7 was captured by 4' to form 1'.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 17
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 17. Sedimentation velocity-based analysis of proteins. The raw sedimentation velocity 
profiles of PycR1 (a) and EupfF (b). For each raw sedimentation velocity profile, the upper panel 
shows the collected data (discrete points) and the fitted data (solid line), corrected for systematic 
noise contributions obtained with absorbance optical system. The colors indicate the evolution in time, 
with early scans in blue and late scans in red. The middle panel shows the residuals of overlay of the 
c(s) fit. The lower panel shows the sedimentation coefficient distributions c(s) of the testing protein 
sample calculated by the program SEDFIT.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 18
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 18. Relative activity of proteins pre-treated with 0-50 mM EDTA disodium salt. The 
fresh purified proteins were dialyzed extensively with buffer containing 0-50 mM (0, 2, 5 10, 20, 50 mM) 
EDTA disodium salt in a 15 ml ultrafiltration device for three times (a-g). The 100 μL reaction mixtures 
containing 50 mM PBS at pH 7.2-7.4, 1 mM 6, 1 mM 4 (4'), and 10 μM EupfF or PycR1 or their variants 
pre-treated with different concentration of EDTA disodium salt, were incubated at 28 °C for 90 min. The 
activities were compared to that of PycR1 (WT, 100%). Black boxes highlight that EupfF and PycR1N211A 
lost most of the activity in the 10 mM EDTA disodium salt. g) PycR1_AN and PycR1_E. coli represent 
protein purified from A. nidulans (AN.) and E. coli, respectively. h) PycR1_E. coli + EDTA represent protein 
pre-treated with 10 mM EDTA disodium salt were added 2-20 mM (2, 5, 10, 15, 20 mM) CaCl2 to recover 
their activity. Enzyme activity values represent mean ± s.d. of three independent replicates.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 19
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 19. Relative activity of wide type DAases and their glycosylation site mutants pre-treated 
with 10 mM EDTA disodium salt. Enzymatic reactions were performed with 1 μM enzymes and 
incubated with 20 μM 6 and 10 μM 4 (4') in the 50 mM PBS buffer at pH 7.2-7.4 for 30 mins. The 
activity of wild type PycR1 to catalyze the formation of 1/1' was set as reference (pink box: relative 
yield of 1 or 1'; light blue box: relative yield of 2 or 2'). To exclude the effect of inherent Ca2+ in the 
proteins, the fresh purified protein samples were dialyzed extensively with buffer containing 10 mM 
EDTA disodium salt in a 15ml ultrafiltration device for three times. For PycR1 and its mutants, 4' 
was used as dienophile and 1'-2' were detected as products. In the cases of EupfF, its mutants, and 
homologs AtDA and ClDA, 4 was used as substrate, and 1-2 were detected as products. Enzyme 
activity values represent mean ± s.d. of three independent replicates. The results showed that only 
glycosylation site mutant PycR1_N211A/Q had significant changes in activity under the influence of 
10 mM EDTA, while the glycosylation site mutants in EupfF (N45A, N68Q, N213Q and N300Q) had 
no changes in activity compared with wide-type EupfF. Homologous proteins AtDA and ClDA have 
similar properties to EupfF.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 20
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 20. Native MS of PycR1, PycR1N211A, and PycR1 N43A. The native MS results show that 
PycR1 (~85 kDa) and PycR1 N43A (~82 kDa) were dimers, while PycR1N211A was mixture of dimer 
(~82 kDa) and monomer (~40 kDa).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 21
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 21. Effects of concentration of Ca2+ and other divalent metal ions on the activity of 
PycR1N211A. The reaction mixtures containing 20 μM 6, 10 μM 2' (a) or 10 μM 4' (b), 1 μM enzymes 
(PycR1 as control, PycR1N211A, or EDTA pre-treated PycR1N211A) in the 50 mM PBS buffer at pH 
7.2-7.4, were incubated at 28 °C for 30 mins. For reactions with EDTA pre-treated PycR1N211A, 
additional 2 mM various divalent metals (Ca2+, Ni2+, Mg2+, Mn2+, Cu2+, Zn2+, Co2+, Fe2+) were added. 
In the complementary experiments of Ca2+, 0.05-5 mM CaCl2 was added to the reaction. Enzyme 
activity values represent mean ± s.d. of three independent replicates.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 22
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 22. PycR1 purified from E. coli. SDS-PAGE gel (12%) shows a MW in 35 kDa. M: protein 
marker of Unstained Protein Molecular Weight Marker (14.4-116 kDa).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 23
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 23. Unfavored transition state (TS) energies for the pycnidione series (a) and the 
eupenifeldin series (b). A) The transition state pyc-TS2 for diastereoisomeric monoadduct 2'-a, and 
pyc-TS4, TS5, TS6 for bis-adducts 1'-a/b/c; B) The transition state eup-TS2 for monoadducts 2-a, 
and eup-TS4, TS5, TS6 for bis-adducts 1-a/b/c. The energies shown in the figure are free energies, 
and were calculated using ωB97X-D/def2-QZVPP//ωB97X-D/def2-SVP.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 24
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 24. The crystal structure of PycR1 in complex with 4'. a) The overall structure of PycR1-
4'. PycR1 was shown in cartoon (colored light blue), and compound 4' is shown in stick form (colored 
wheat). For simplicity, glycan chains are not shown. b) Enlarged view of the interactions between 4' 
and its surrounding residues. The interactions presented as yellow dashed lines. N341, N228, D275, 
E48, and Q158, the Ca2+, and the surrounding waters form a large water molecule (colored red) 
network through hydrogen bond. c) The omit map of 4', which was modeled into an electron density 
(Fo-Fc map, white), contoured to 3.0 σ.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 25
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 25. Active pocket of PycR1. A large substrate-binding cavity is showed next to the Ca2+. The 
volume of the cavity was calculated using POCASA software.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 26
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 26. Superposition of PycR1 complex and unliganded PycR1. a) Superposition of the 
PycR1-4' complex (colored as in light blue) with unliganded PycR1 colored in white. Substantial 
conformational changes are observed for M119, M342, and V352. The distance between two 
positions of the Ca ions is 0.4 Å. b) Superposition of the PycR1-2-7 complex (residues, light blue; 
compound 2, yellow; compound 7, green) with unliganded PycR1 colored in white. Substantial 
conformational changes are observed for M119 and M342. The distance between two positions of the 
Ca ions is 0.2 Å.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 27
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 27. Superposition of compounds and Ca2+ in crystal complex PycR1-2-7 and PycR1-4'. 
Compound 2 (yellow), 7 (green) and Ca2+ (violet) were showed in PycR1-2-7. Compound 4' (wheat) 
and Ca2+ (violet) were showed in PycR1-4'. Compound 4' and the eleven-numbered ring of 2 occupy 
almost the same position in the cavity of PycR1. Two calcium ions are in the same position.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 28
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 28. Superposition of pyc-TS3 (yellow) in PycR1 and crystal complex PycR1-2-7 (Pink). 
Compound 2', 7 and Ca2+ were showed in PycR1- pyc-TS3 (colored yellow and light yellow). 
Compound 2, 7 and Ca2+ were showed in complex PycR1-2-7 (colored pink and light pink). 
Substantial conformational changes are observed for Y176, V225, N228. In which, N228 binds with 
Ca2+, while V225 form a hydrogen bond with the 10-hydroxyl of monoadduct 2' and Y176 interact 
with 7. The distance between the V225 and the 10-hydroxyl of 2' in PycR1- pyc-TS3 is 3.4 Å, while 
the distance between the V225 and the 10-hydroxyl of 2 in complex PycR1-2-7 is 4.8 Å. The residues 
W46, S63, R94, N293 that interact with 7 and the seven-numbered ring of 2/2' occupy almost the 
same position in the cavity. The distance between two positions of the Ca ions is 1.5 Å.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 29
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 29. MD simulations of the Y176A and Y176F mutant with pyc-TS1. The top shows the 
hydrogen bond length between Oxygen 2 in 7 and R94 in the simulations for WT and Y176A/F PycR1. 
The bottom left shows the representative structure of pyc-TS1 in Y176A PycR1. The bottom right 
shows a representative structure of pyc-TS1 in Y176F within the 800-900 ns simulation. The results 
indicate that removal of the phenyl group (i.e., the Y176A mutation) destabilizes the hydrogen bond 
between Oxygen 2 in 7 and R94.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 30
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 30. MD simulation of mutation of K341 and S242 in active cavity of PycR1. a) MD 
simulation of pyc-TS3 with the N341K mutant. The left structure was obtained upon docking and 
after minimization and equilibrium processing. The right structure is the representative structure of 
the 1000 ns production simulation. b) MD simulations of the S242M mutant with pyc-TS3. The top 
middle shows the hydrogen bond length between Oxygen 4 in 2' and V225 in the simulation of WT 
and S242M. The bottom left shows the representative structure of pyc-TS3 in WT. The bottom right 
shows the representative structure of pyc-TS3 in S242M PycR1. Introduction of the bulky thiomethyl 
group change the loop near V225, making V225 far apart from Oxygen 4 in 2', and breaking this 
hydrogen bond.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 31
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 31. EupfF from Penicillium janthinellum was a secreted protein with TDA catalytic 
activity. a) LC-MS analysis of crude extraction of Penicillium janthinellum after culture in PDB 
medium for 7 days. b) SDS-PAGE gel (12%) of AN-EupfF (purified from A. nidulans strains) and 
broth of Penicillium janthinellum. M: protein marker of Prestained Protein Ladder from 
PageRulerTM, product #26616. The band marked in red was excised, and then it was verified as 
EupfF containing glycans by LC-MS/MS analysis (see Supplementary Table 10-11). c) In vitro 
analysis of EupfF (A. nidulans strains) and broth of Penicillium janthinellum using 4 and 6 as 
substrates. d) The reaction scheme to form compound 1.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 32
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 32. Sequence network analysis and phylogenetic analysis of EupfF and its homologous. 
a) To construct a sequence similarity networks, a blast search of EupfF was carried out in UniProt 
database and a total of 981 sequences were retrieved. An all-by-all BLAST (e-value threshold was 
set to 70) was performed to obtain the similarities between sequence pairs to calculate edge values 
and generate the SSN. Cytoscape was used to visualization of SSNs. b) Phylogenetic tree was 
constructed by MEGA using the homologous sequences clustered with EupfF in SSNs, together 
with reported EupR1 from Phaeosphaeriaceae sp. and PycR1 from Leptobacillium sp.. The 
homologous sequences from strain Aspergilllus thermomutatus and Cytospora leucostoma were 
renamed as AtDA (A0A397GLM8) and ClDA (A0A423W557), respectively.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 33
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 33. Alignment of the BGCs containing EupfF or its homologous. Alignment was created 
using Clinker and Clustermap.js. The homologs of EupfF included EupF (Phoma sp.), AsR5 
(Sarocladium sp.), ClDA (Cytospora leucostoma), AtDA (Aspergilllus thermomutatus), TpDA 
(Tolypociadium paradoxum), and MrDA (Metarhizium rileyi RCEF 4871). Parallel line in BGC 
encoding AtDA was used to connect the clusters of genes that may separate during sequencing and 
assembly of the genome.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 34
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 34. The homologues of EupfF. (a). SDS-PAGE gel (12%) of mycelium and broth of A. 
nidulans strains co-expressing the genes encoded AtDA and ClDA, respectively. M: protein marker 
of Prestained Protein Ladder from PageRulerTM, product #26616.  (b). LC-MS analysis of the 
products from in vitro assays of AtDA, ClDA and EupfF using 6 and 2 (or 4) as substrates. The 100 μL 
reaction mixtures containing 50 mM PBS at pH 7.2-7.4, 1 mM pre-diene 6, 1 mM 4 or 2, 50 μM 
EupfF or ClDA or AtDA were incubated at 28 °C for 90 min. The reactions were terminated by the 
addition of 400 ml of EtOAc and were extracted for three times. The supernatants were concentrated 
by vacuum and then dissolved in 30 μl MeOH before analyzed by UPLC/MS. The results showed 
that ClDA and AtDA were similar to EupfF, and also possess the catalytic activity for TDA reaction.

(ROV98449.1), AsR5 (AWM95794.1), EupR1, and PycR1 are derived from Phoma sp., Aspergillus 
thermomutatus, Cytospora leucostoma, Sarocladium schorii, Leptobacillium sp., and
